title: Re-slice 0005: three cases closed, three decisions open

closed.cause: The retry backoff waits on a token linked from the caller token and the stopping token, so a cancellation raised there carried neither. The stopping branch was unreachable and the caller received a TaskCanceledException bound to a token it had never seen.
closed.fix: src/ViciOne.ServiceBus/Transports/HostConfigurationRetryExtensions.cs asks the sources instead of the exception.
closed.assertionChange: strengthened, not relaxed: the cancellation must now also carry the caller's token

closed.cause: No ActivityListener, so Activity.Current is null: AddBaggage did nothing and the publish handler's filter could never match. The round trip itself completed in 39 ms and the test still waited out 30 s.
closed.fix: The spec registers an ActivityListener in SetUp and disposes it in TearDown. No production file changed.

closed.cause: JobService.Stop set a stopping flag and nothing ever cleared it. BusStarted restored the heartbeat but not the flag, so a restarted service rejected every StartJob with JobServiceStoppingException, forever.
closed.proof: green in isolation, exit 0; the rejection loop is gone from the log

closed.case: Masking defect found on the way, not one of the five
closed.cause: Both connection close sites in RabbitMqTestHarnessHostedService passed an exception message as the AMQP close reason. That field holds 255 bytes, so a longer message overflowed the frame buffer and threw an encoding ArgumentException from inside the catch handler, replacing the real failure. Eight job specs reported an encoding error for a harness start that had failed for a different reason.
closed.fix: The reason is trimmed on character boundaries and a failed close is logged instead of replacing the outcome.
closed.proof: the eight specs now run a full minute and fail on their real cause instead of 40 ms of encoding error

openDecisions.measured: A real defect was found and fixed on the way: connecting a consumer to a bus whose on-demand endpoint can never start blocked the caller forever, unbounded and uncancellable, at three call sites. That is corrected and bound by BusEndpointReady_Specs, red before and green after. The spec itself still fails identically: Expected <RabbitMqConnectionException>, but was: no exception thrown.
openDecisions.why: The spec asserts that Start() throws. The bus endpoint is materialised on demand, so Start() never claims the exclusive queue and cannot detect the conflict. Green requires either declaring the bus endpoint eagerly, which changes intended messaging semantics, or moving and retyping the assertion, which is a rewrite. Upstream MassTransit carries the same spec as [Explicit], so the expectation never ran against a broker there either. That is provenance, not a disposition.
openDecisions.decision: Whether on-demand materialisation is intended, and if so what the spec should assert instead.

openDecisions.measured: The consumer never runs at all: zero 'Processing batch' entries. The batch waits for its 80 second time limit because six messages are published against a message limit of ten, while the endpoint sets a delivery acknowledgement timeout of ten seconds. The broker closes the channel every ten seconds: 'PRECONDITION_FAILED - delivery acknowledgement on channel 2 timed out. Timeout value used: 10000 ms.'
openDecisions.why: Nothing in the product reconciles a batch time limit with the delivery acknowledgement timeout: no validation, no clamping. Closing this means either adding that reconciliation, which changes the RabbitMQ configuration contract, or changing the spec's own numbers, which changes the scenario.
openDecisions.dependencyQuestionAnswered: Re-slice 0005 item 7 is settled: the ConnectionClose.WriteTo error was a symptom of the masking defect above, not a client defect that forces a version change. RabbitMQ.Client stays at 7.2.1 and Directory.Packages.props is untouched.
openDecisions.decision: Whether the product should reconcile the two settings, or the spec's configuration is wrong.

openDecisions.case: Isolation of the job restart spec
openDecisions.measured: Enabling the restart spec broke seven sibling specs plus JobDistributionStrategy_Specs with 'ReceiveTransport faulted', close-reason 491, 'ObjectDisposedException on channel'. A bisect with that one spec filtered out leaves the siblings green. Measured cause: the spec drives the hosted service lifecycle by hand and leaves one connection open at the broker after the explicit stop, which RabbitMQ.Client recovers automatically into the virtual host the next spec has just cleaned.
openDecisions.attempted: Giving the spec its own virtual host removes the interference: the seven siblings pass. The spec itself then fails, because a freshly created virtual host is cold and its ten second completion budget no longer covers the retry delay of about three seconds plus the five second job.
openDecisions.why: Raising that budget is a timeout extension and is forbidden. Keeping the shared virtual host keeps the interference. Both remaining levers are decisions.
openDecisions.decision: Shared virtual host with the interference, isolated virtual host with a budget that fits it, or another isolation.

gateState.why: D3 in the shared virtual host; D1 and D2 remain unlisted and unexecuted by design.

notWeakened: No assertion was relaxed; one was strengthened.
No filter was introduced in the required path.
No [Ignore] was added; three [Explicit] were removed so cases run.
No case was reclassified as not due.
